study.question: Does the small conditional utility of explicit historical membership depend on cross-row Dice normalization, or can aligned membership content benefit click through auxiliary readouts when primary scorer normalization is row-local?
study.hypothesis: Native full-minus-counts click AUC is +0.0000604314, reverses to -0.0000883776 with balanced stratum masses, remains +0.0000858490 with feedback Dice-input gradients blocked, and shrinks to +0.0000134479 when auxiliary feedback bases are replaced by uniform bases. The last counts-only algebraic negative control itself moves -0.0000243537, so this is unresolved pathway evidence, not confirmed mediation. Feedback means influence the native primary uniform readout through cross-row Dice statistics, even though click reads only uniform strata. Replacing ONLY primary scorer Dice normalization by per-row channel normalization eliminates that coupling; full/counts then differ directly in auxiliary feedback histories while click uniform scorer rows are independent of feedback rows at fixed weights. Predict that the full-minus-counts gain shrinks if native utility mainly needs cross-row normalization. A remaining positive difference would motivate a follow-up on the auxiliary context-transfer route. Masks are deterministic action-task-table functions of historical action codes in the inspected loader, so any utility is representational or optimization utility, not extra conditional information.

nearest_work.difference: Primary text lines 260-285 describes target-conditioned local activation; lines 317-336 describes Dice with training batch moments and test moving moments. Inherit target-conditioned scorer and learned alpha but replace only its cross-row normalization with a standard per-row channel-normalized sigmoid gate. This is a pathway control, not a new normalization or DIN reproduction claim.

Pinned lines 25-34 implement Dice as affine-free BatchNorm1d, eps=1e-9, momentum=0.01, and learned channel alpha. New scorer uses that same alpha and epsilon with FP32 per-row mean and biased variance, retaining original modules and state for exact capacity matching. Tower Dice and unused auxiliary scorer remain native.

Pinned lines 123-170 initialize one sequence hub per task using task masks, then mix categorical, sequential and task tokens. No hubs or broadcasts are adopted; isolate use of the incumbent auxiliary-union membership under two scorer normalizations.
Original paper has provenance/link only in authorized registry; detailed original text unavailable there. No original-paper reproduction, priority or equivalence claim.

inherited_components: Unchanged strongest full-membership utility control and its exact counts-only replacement; all item fields, target inputs, aligned historical actions and valid-event order.

Same joint four-true-label BCE, auxiliary item/scorer detach ownership, private auxiliary learning, and inherited occupied-cycle source-bit surrogate context VJP; this VJP is not the ordinary joint-BCE derivative.
Same model construction order, parameter initialization, RNG, registered state keys and dormant auxiliary scorer pass. Same fixed one-pass training protocol and validation population.
study.proposed_difference: A 2x2 replacement design: explicit membership content {full, counts-only} crossed with primary scorer normalization {native cross-row Dice, row-local channel normalization}. In row-local arms use sigmoid((x-row_mean)/sqrt(row_biased_variance+native_eps)) with inherited per-channel alpha. Accumulate normalization moments in FP32 then cast gate to input dtype; host BF16 autocast stays frozen. Apply at each primary scorer Dice in folded training and pruned evaluation, retain 70-row Dice expansion in training, and leave all tower and unused auxiliary scorer Dice native. No new learned modules, buffers, input features or scorer passes. Native arms are byte-identical ancestor copies. This tests a conditional pathway under a replacement representation; it does not estimate a pure natural indirect effect in the native network.
predictions: At a common parameter state in row-local arms, changing only membership full to counts cannot affect click logits: uniform compressed rows and all click detail channels are unchanged and scorer operations couple channels within each row only. Auxiliary logits can differ. This is a host prerequisite before interpreting training results.

If native membership benefit needs cross-row moments, delta_local=AUC(full_local)-AUC(counts_local) should be smaller than delta_native, with interaction delta_local-delta_native negative. Sign alone at one fixed seed is preliminary.
If auxiliary readout content is sufficient under the replacement, delta_local should remain positive and survive a future matched valid-event membership-permutation control and paired repetitions.
Learned parameter counts must remain 32192421 (31793216 embedding,399205 dense). Runtime, latency and peak memory can change despite equal capacity; any cost improvement must be measured.
falsifiers: At fixed common weights, row-local click predictions or uniform pooled histories depend on full versus counts-only membership beyond measured numerical tolerance: implementation or numerical independence prerequisite fails; do not interpret AUC as pathway evidence.
delta_local matches/exceeds delta_native reproducibly with valid negative controls: the proposed dependence on cross-row moments is unsupported under this replacement.

Both row-local arms suffer large comparable quality collapse, or numerical perturbations/seed variation are as large as the interaction: pathway result is inconclusive, not a refutation of membership utility.
Changed parameters, state initialization, input visibility, BCE supervision, gradient ownership or training exposure invalidates the intended comparison.
alternative_explanations: Row-local channel normalization changes scorer geometry, amplitude sensitivity and inductive bias, not merely moment support; an interaction may depend on this changed optimization environment.
Native BF16 split-sum arithmetic produced a measurable counts-only negative-control shift in the prior readout experiment; comparable tiny effects may reflect arithmetic trajectory sensitivity.
One frozen train_seed is available here; deterministic bridge reruns are not independent random-seed repetitions or independent mechanism contrasts.
Auxiliary context VJP transfers batch-level surrogate directions, so utility may be regularization through auxiliary optimization rather than semantically useful per-user event assignment.
Masks encode an auxiliary union in this model, not separate task-bit identities; no claim about all possible mask representations or production-time feedback availability.
Equal learned parameter counts do not match execution cost or effective function classes. Offline labels match user/category/brand within 24h, not ad-attributed conversions.
